Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain relief from breathing issues; understand cause
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage physical respiratory condition; monitor for emerging anxiety
- Actions (Patient): Attend in-person GP assessment; obtain peak flow/oxygen saturation check; consider OTC antihistamine as advised
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Perform objective respiratory evaluation; educate patient on asthma management; screen for anxiety at follow-up

Secondary Problem (Anxiety related to health concern):
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce worry about breathing
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide reassurance; assess need for further mental health support if anxiety persists
- Actions (Patient): Practice paced breathing; follow medical advice
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Reassess anxiety levels after physical condition addressed; provide psychoeducation or brief intervention if required

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Use of antihistamines; need for objective respiratory testing; possible need for inhaler/steroids
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased breathlessness, inability to finish sentences, nighttime worsening
- Coping Strategies: Seek urgent care if severe breathlessness; use inhaler if prescribed; relaxation breathing
